metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast spikes; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.7) and price has recently spiked, model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 3–7 days.
- Model consistently under-forecasts sharp upward moves (e.g., >40% from prior low) in the 1–3 day horizon; apply +5–10% bias to short-term forecasts when sentiment is bullish.
- Model over-forecasts in the 7–14 day horizon after a spike; apply -5–10% correction if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; add +3–7% bias to forecast from day 5 onward if sentiment turns positive.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 3+ days, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5 days unless sentiment is strong bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.6) and price is volatile, model tends to over-smooth; increase forecast volatility by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
